doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Eddie Vinson and the Pacific Brass Band
title: Giggy Williams, Billy Moran and the Matthews drummer brothers
summary: Russell asks about guitarist Norwood 'Giggy' Williams, whom neither man remembers. Martin recalls Billy Moran on bass and the four Matthews brothers, all drummers, including Bebe 'Tyke' and Remus.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I met a guitar player out in Los Angeles, oh twenty years or more ago, twenty-five years ago. And they called him Giggy Williams. His real name is Norwood Williams.

Norwood Williams. He was with that band out on the road. I don't know if he played with them here, but he came from, do you remember him, a guitar player? Did he? No, Giggy. G-I-G-I is the way I spelled it. Giggy. Giggy Williams. Norwood Williams was his real name. Williams.
I guess he left here so long ago that most people didn't remember him here.

When he left here in 16, Billy Moran was playing drum, playing bass with him. Billy Moran, yeah. That's right. Billy Moran was playing bass with that bunch. With that bunch, but they left. Yeah. But Billy Moran didn't leave. He stayed here. He stayed here. You know, let's see, Bebe was beating drum for me. Bebe Matthews? That's right. Oh, yeah. Bebe was beating drums. What was his last name? That's his name, Bebe Matthews. Oh, Matthews.
But they was calling him Tyke. His nickname, they called him Tyke.
Yeah, I never knew him. I knew Bill Matthews as the only brother I knew.
Well, they had four of them, and all of them was drummers.
And one of them worked on the boat, and I didn't even know it. That was Remus. Remus, yeah. I guess I saw him a lot of times, didn't even know it.
And he was a good drummer, too.
Yeah, I wish I'd talk to him. He didn't play those last years, I guess.
No, he stopped. The last time he played was in the Island Band.
